findings.title: Stray duplicate test file committed with stale factory signature
findings.description: A 146-line backup/editor artifact (`CoreServiceFactory.test.ts-E`, blob `e6539010`, identical to the pre-change version of `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts`) was added to the repo in this changeset. It still calls `createContextPipeline(FIXTURE_PROJECT_PATH)` with the old single-argument signature, i.e. it is a stale, non-compiling duplicate of code that was just changed. It is inert today — vitest's include pattern (`tests/**/*.{test,spec}.*`) never selects it, `packages/core/tsconfig.json` only typechecks `src/**/*`, and the root eslint config ignores `**/tests/**` — so it can't fail CI. But it is dead code in the test tree that will confuse the next reader and would become a compile error the moment tests are typechecked. Delete the file; nothing else references it.

findings.title: Adoption resolver: clear step discipline, typed errors, no silent fallbacks
findings.description: The 6-step flow (phase gate with no I/O → persisted state → planning artifacts → bounded source walk → guide capability check → state write → fact rendering) is implemented in one place as the header comment promises, with `decide()` reading each fact only when the previous didn't decide, and `persistInProgress` converting write failures into `AdoptionError` with a concrete remedy instead of building anyway. Exhaustive `never` switches on the outcome union fail loudly on future kinds. I verified the surrounding contracts (`adoptionOutcome.ts`, `adoptionFacts.ts`, `adoptionState.ts`) and detection modules; the unit and integration test matrices (selection, read-only, overrides, guide-missing, monorepo scoping, shallow clone) match the implementation's behavior on every path I traced.

findings.title: Integrator/engine changes are behavior-preserving when adoption is not selected
findings.description: When the resolver returns `{ selected: false }`, the project is mapped untouched and `adoptionFacts` is never set, so output is identical to before (the `not selected: data is identical to an integrator without a resolver` test pins this with a date normalization). The engine's new section (order 3.4, between instruction prompt and the 3.5 permissiveness fragment) only renders for non-blank `adoptionFacts`, and the `it.each` baseline test confirms byte-identity for empty/whitespace/undefined values. `AdoptionStateWrites` being a required option on `createContextPipeline` forces every caller to decide explicitly, which is the right shape for the persist/read-only split.

findings.title: CLI/MCP write-mode split is correct and parity-tested
findings.description: `context_build` uses `persist`, `template_preview` uses `read-only` (matching its documented "without side effects" contract and `readOnlyHint: true`), and the CLI uses `persist`. The new `adoptionParity.test.ts` runs both real paths (MCP tool over InMemoryTransport and the CLI's pipeline+integrator sequence) against one checkout and asserts byte-identical prompts, resetting `.context-forge.toml` between them so both start from the same inputs — a strong guard against the two paths drifting. The unit tests in `contextTools.test.ts` and `build.test.ts` pin the exact options object each tool passes.
